A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICPT work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-E are readable and support reliable matching despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original personalization experiments across four LVLM backbones, ablations, qualitative examples, latency measurements, and training-data analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds evaluations on four public personalization benchmarks in Table 3.

M1.justification: The ACP, DTR, CVM, MCS, frozen-backbone procedure, and training losses remain unchanged in Section 3. Corrections to diagram labels do not alter the method.

E1.justification: v2 adds separate evaluations on the public Yo’LLaVA, MyVLM, MC-LLaVA, and MMPB benchmarks. v1 already used concepts from these sources within its customized evaluation, so this extends benchmark coverage within the existing personalization domain without introducing a new task family.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched experiments. New Table 3 reuses ICL, PLVM, and MC-LLaVA, abbreviated MC-L; it introduces no new comparison method.

E3.justification: The added public-benchmark evaluations exclude ICPT training concepts from Yo’LLaVA, MyVLM, and MC-LLaVA and report averages across models. These are protocols for additional experiments; the original evaluation and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, sensitivity studies, qualitative examples, failure analysis, efficiency analysis, and volume-versus-diversity study are retained. Figure 3's new reference to failure-case analyses points to discussion already present in v1 Appendix E.1.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the reported comparisons. Table 3's averaging across models does not introduce experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports ICPT scores of 0.926, 0.972, 0.915, and 0.853 on Yo’LLaVA, MyVLM, MC-LLaVA, and MMPB, respectively, exceeding the listed comparators. Matched original tables, plots, and qualitative findings are unchanged; these are additional benchmark results, not same-setting performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, geometric constraints, State-Induced Interference Bound, and Appendix B proof are unchanged, including their assumptions and derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient multi-image, multi-concept personalization, geometric regularization, and performance across LVLM backbones. The added benchmark evidence supports those existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 now interprets the public-benchmark results as showing that ICPT's advantage extends beyond the customized evaluation. Existing mechanism explanations and limitations concerning visually similar concepts and numerous labels remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a limited data-processing instruction for the new benchmark results: remove concepts overlapping ICPT training from the first three benchmarks. Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, software, and resource-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Li et al., Multimodal Foundation Models: From Specialists to General-Purpose Assistants, as introduction background. The related-work discussion and substantive positioning against prior personalization methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 corrects placeholder running headers, adds affiliation countries and a corresponding-author designation, adjusts title capitalization, and inserts a benchmark-results paragraph. Most prose and the section and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds compact Table 3, relocates Figure 3 and several existing displays, and renumbers the appendix tables. Figures 1-2 receive label corrections, and Figure 3's caption gains an appendix pointer; existing result plots remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Table 3 adds useful validation beyond the customized test set, while corrected figure labels and running headers improve presentation. The gain is limited because the added comparison does not clearly specify its metrics, retained evaluation counts, or precise cross-model aggregation. The method and existing evidence remain intact.
